title: Marisol and the Shy Cloud
blurb: The farm is dry and the rain will not come. Marisol finds a small cloud that is hiding on her roof.

chapters.title: A Thirsty Farm
chapters.text:
It had not rained for forty days in the little village where Marisol lived in Brazil. The ground was cracked like an old plate. The corn leaves hung down, tired and yellow. Even the old dog slept under the cart all day with his tongue out.

Every morning, Marisol's father looked at the sky and sighed. "Not a single cloud," he said. He picked up a handful of soil and let it run through his fingers like sand. Marisol's mother said nothing, but she put less water in the soup pot.

Before school, Marisol carried water from the well to the garden. The buckets were heavy, and the sun was hot. She gave one cup to each bean plant, and she counted so that it would be fair. The well was getting low. The bucket had to go down a long way before it splashed.

"Please, rain, come soon," she whispered.

That night, the house was hot and still, and she could not sleep. Then she heard a strange sound on the roof. It was not the cat. It was not the wind, because there was no wind. It was a soft, sniffly noise, like someone trying not to cry.

questions.prompt: Where does Marisol live?
options: In Brazil
In Argentina
In Portugal
In Mexico
questions.why: The first sentence says Marisol lived in a little village in Brazil.

questions.prompt: How long had it not rained?
options: Four days
Fourteen days
Forty days
Four hundred days
questions.why: It had not rained for forty days.

questions.prompt: What did the ground look like?
options: It was soft and covered with grass
It was hidden under yellow corn leaves
It was deep in sticky brown mud
It was cracked like an old plate
questions.why: The ground was cracked like an old plate.

questions.prompt: Why did Marisol's mother put less water in the soup pot?
options: The family did not like soup
Water was running short
The soup was already too thin
The pot had a hole in it
questions.why: There had been no rain for forty days and the well was getting low, so the family had to save water.

questions.prompt: Why did Marisol count the cups of water?
options: She wanted each bean plant to have a fair share
Her teacher had given her a sum to practise
Her father paid her for every cup she carried
She wanted to know how heavy the buckets were
questions.why: She gave one cup to each bean plant, and she counted so that it would be fair.

questions.prompt: How could Marisol tell that the well was getting low?
options: Her father put a sign on the well to warn her
The rope was too short to touch the water
The water in the bucket had turned yellow
The bucket went down a long way before it splashed
questions.why: The bucket had to go down a long way before it splashed.

questions.prompt: What did Marisol hear at night?
options: The cat fighting with the old dog
A soft, sniffly noise on the roof
A loud clap of thunder in the hills
Wind blowing through the corn
questions.why: It was a soft, sniffly noise, like someone trying not to cry. The text says it was not the cat or the wind.

chapters.title: The Cloud on the Roof
chapters.text:
Marisol took a torch and climbed the ladder. The rungs were still warm from the day. On the roof sat a small grey cloud, no bigger than a sofa. It was curled up in a ball with its edges shaking. It smelled of wet stones.

"Are you a cloud?" asked Marisol. It was a silly question, but she could not think of another one.

"Yes," sniffed the cloud. "My name is Nimbo."

"Why are you not up in the sky?" asked Marisol. "We need rain so much. The corn is dying, and the well is nearly empty."

Nimbo hid its face. "I cannot make rain," it said. "I am too shy. Rain is noisy. It drums, it splashes, and everyone looks at me."

Marisol thought of her father, staring at the sky each morning. It was true. Everyone would look.

She sat down next to Nimbo. The roof tiles were hard, but the cloud felt cool against her arm, and that was lovely after the hot day. She did not laugh. "Everyone is waiting for you," she said gently. "Maybe I can help."

One grey edge lifted a little. "How?" asked Nimbo.

"I do not know yet," said Marisol. "But I carry heavy buckets every day. Perhaps I can carry some of your worry, too."

questions.prompt: What did Marisol take with her up the ladder?
options: A blanket
A bucket
A rope
A torch
questions.why: Marisol took a torch and climbed the ladder.

questions.prompt: How big was the cloud?
options: As big as the whole farm
No bigger than a sofa
As tall as the corn plants
As small as a tennis ball
questions.why: The text says it was a small grey cloud, no bigger than a sofa.

questions.prompt: What did the cloud smell of?
options: Corn leaves
Fresh bread
Wet stones
Burnt wood
questions.why: It smelled of wet stones.

questions.prompt: Why could Nimbo not make rain?
options: It was too shy
It was too tired
It was too high up
It was too young
questions.why: Nimbo said, "I cannot make rain. I am too shy."

questions.prompt: What did Nimbo dislike about rain?
options: Rain is noisy, and everyone looks at it
Rain makes the roof tiles slippery
Rain makes the corn grow far too tall
Rain is much too cold for a small cloud
questions.why: Nimbo said rain drums and splashes, and everyone looks at it.

questions.prompt: Why did the cloud's cool side feel lovely to Marisol?
options: She liked the smell of the roof
She had a bad fever that night
The day had been very hot
She had just been swimming
questions.why: The text says the cloud felt cool, and that was lovely after the hot day.

questions.prompt: How does the text show that Marisol is kind?
options: She gives Nimbo a cup of water from the well
She does not laugh at Nimbo, and she speaks gently
She tells Nimbo that shy clouds are silly
She runs to fetch her father to meet Nimbo
questions.why: She did not laugh, and she said gently that she might be able to help.

questions.prompt: What does Marisol mean when she talks about carrying Nimbo's worry?
options: She wants to take Nimbo away to her school
She thinks Nimbo is too heavy to float
She plans to lift Nimbo down in a bucket
She wants to help make Nimbo's fear feel lighter
questions.why: She compares the worry with her heavy buckets. She means that she can share the problem, because a worry cannot really be carried in the hands.

chapters.title: Three Silly Tricks
chapters.text:
The next morning, before the sun grew too hot, Marisol tried to help Nimbo. She wrote her plan on her hand: song, feather, joke.

First, she sang the loudest song she knew. "Rain, rain, fall on the corn!" The chickens ran away, and the old dog howled along. Nimbo only shook. "Too loud," it whispered. It did not rain.

Next, she found a long feather and tickled the cloud. Nimbo giggled, and a few tiny drops fell. Marisol held her breath. One drop, two drops, three! But then the cat sneezed, and Nimbo jumped and stopped.

Last, she told the funniest joke she knew. "Why did the cloud go to school? To get a little brighter!" Nimbo laughed so hard that it rolled off the roof and bounced across the yard. Not a drop fell. It floated back up, looking very pleased with itself.

By now the sun was high, and the corn looked worse than ever.

"It is no use," said Marisol. "Tricks do not work." She sat on the step, and she thought and thought. A trick could make Nimbo forget to be shy for a moment. But the moment always ended, and the shy feeling came back. She needed something that would last.

questions.prompt: Where did Marisol write her plan?
options: On her hand
On the kitchen wall
In her school book
On the roof tiles
questions.why: She wrote her plan on her hand: song, feather, joke.

questions.prompt: In what order did Marisol try her tricks?
options: Joke, song, feather
Feather, joke, song
Song, feather, joke
Song, joke, feather
questions.why: First she sang, next she used the feather, and last she told a joke.

questions.prompt: Why did the loud song fail?
options: Nimbo could not hear it from the roof
The old dog howled and drowned out the song
Marisol had forgotten the words of the song
It frightened Nimbo instead of helping
questions.why: Nimbo only shook and whispered, "Too loud." Noise is what it fears, so the song made things worse.

questions.prompt: What happened when Marisol tickled Nimbo?
options: Nimbo grew as large as the farmhouse
Nimbo giggled, and a few tiny drops fell
Nimbo floated away over the hills
Nimbo sneezed, and a big storm began
questions.why: Nimbo giggled, and a few tiny drops fell. She counted three.

questions.prompt: Why did the tiny drops stop?
options: Marisol's arm grew too tired to tickle
The sun came out from behind the hill
The cat sneezed, and Nimbo jumped
The feather broke in Marisol's hand
questions.why: But then the cat sneezed, and Nimbo jumped and stopped.

questions.prompt: What happened after the joke?
options: Nimbo told a funnier joke of its own
A heavy rain fell for a short time
Nimbo felt hurt and hid behind the well
Nimbo rolled off the roof, and no rain fell
questions.why: Nimbo laughed so hard that it rolled off the roof, and not a drop fell.

questions.prompt: What did Marisol work out on the step?
options: Tricks help only for a moment, and she needs something that lasts
The corn will be fine if she carries more water
A louder song would work if she tried it at night
Nimbo does not really want to make any rain at all
questions.why: A trick could make Nimbo forget to be shy for a moment, but the shy feeling came back. She needed something that would last.

chapters.title: A Whisper Instead of a Shout
chapters.text:
That evening, Marisol sat beside Nimbo and watched the first star appear. For a long time, neither of them said anything.

"I get shy too," Marisol said at last.

"You?" asked Nimbo. "But you sang so loudly today."

"That was only for the chickens," said Marisol. "When my teacher asks me to read aloud, my voice shakes and my face gets hot."

Nimbo moved a little closer. "What do you do?" it asked.

"I take a slow breath. I read very softly at first, just for the person next to me. Then, little by little, my voice grows stronger."

Nimbo thought about it. Its edges curled and uncurled. "Soft?" it asked. "Can rain be soft?"

"Soft rain is the best kind," said Marisol. "It does not scare anyone. It does not wash the seeds away. It sinks into the earth, and the roots drink it slowly. And you could begin in the dark, when the village is asleep. Nobody would be looking."

Nimbo took a deep breath, just as she had said, in and out. It floated up from the roof, a little way and then a little further. Its edges stopped shaking.

"Will you stay there?" it called down.

"I will stay," said Marisol. And she did.

questions.prompt: What did Marisol watch that evening?
options: The rising moon
The first star
A flock of birds
A rainbow over the hill
questions.why: She watched the first star appear.

questions.prompt: Why was Nimbo surprised that Marisol gets shy?
options: She was much bigger than Nimbo
She had climbed the ladder in the dark
She had sung very loudly that day
She had a lot of friends at school
questions.why: Nimbo asked, "You? But you sang so loudly today."

questions.prompt: What makes Marisol feel shy?
options: Carrying water to the garden
Singing to the chickens
Talking to her father
Reading aloud in class
questions.why: When her teacher asks her to read aloud, her voice shakes and her face gets hot.

questions.prompt: How does Marisol begin when she feels shy?
options: With a slow breath and a soft voice
With her eyes shut and her hands up
With a long drink of cold water
With a loud shout and a quick joke
questions.why: She takes a slow breath and reads very softly at first.

questions.prompt: Why does Marisol say that soft rain is the best kind?
options: It makes a lovely loud noise on the roof
It sinks in, and the roots drink it slowly
It washes all the seeds down to the river
It falls only on the farms that need it
questions.why: It sinks into the earth, and the roots drink it slowly. She also says it does not wash the seeds away.

questions.prompt: Why does Marisol suggest that Nimbo begins in the dark?
options: The corn drinks water only during the night
Rain can only fall after the first star appears
Clouds are too hard to see in the daytime
Nimbo hates being looked at, and nobody would be watching
questions.why: Nimbo's fear is that everyone looks at it. Marisol says that with the village asleep, nobody would be looking.

questions.prompt: Why does Marisol tell Nimbo about her own shyness?
options: To explain why she does not like her teacher
To make Nimbo feel sorry for her
To show that shy people can still do hard things
To ask Nimbo to read aloud in her class
questions.why: She shares what she does when she is shy, and then Nimbo tries the same thing. Her story shows that being shy does not have to stop you.

chapters.title: The Softest Rain
chapters.text:
Nimbo drifted high above the village. The whole valley was dark and quiet. Marisol stood on the roof with her head back. For a long time, nothing happened. Then came a tiny sound, pit, pit, pit. A single drop fell on Marisol's nose. Then another, and another.

Soon a soft, silver rain was falling over the farm. It tapped on the roofs. It tickled the leaves. The smell of wet earth rose all around her, and the cracked ground drank every drop.

Lights came on, one after another. Marisol's father ran outside with his arms wide open. "Rain!" he shouted. "Marisol, look!" Her mother came out too, holding up the soup pot to catch the drops. Neighbours stood in the road and stared at the sky.

The rain slowed. Marisol held her breath. "Slow breath," she whispered upwards. "Nice and soft."

Then the rain grew a little stronger, steady and sure. High in the sky, a small grey cloud winked at her. The rain fell all night.

In the morning, the corn stood tall and green, and the bucket splashed almost as soon as it went down the well. Marisol had made a friend, and Nimbo was not shy any more. And the next time her teacher asked her to read, she took a slow breath and began.

questions.prompt: What was the first sound of the rain?
options: Splash, splash, splash
Drip, drop, drip
Pit, pit, pit
Boom, boom, boom
questions.why: Then came a tiny sound, pit, pit, pit.

questions.prompt: Where did the first drop land?
options: On the old dog
On the soup pot
On the corn
On Marisol's nose
questions.why: A single drop fell on Marisol's nose.

questions.prompt: What did Marisol's mother do when the rain came?
options: She held up the soup pot to catch the drops
She carried the old dog into the house
She ran to close all the kitchen windows
She stayed asleep inside the dark house
questions.why: Her mother came out too, holding up the soup pot to catch the drops.

questions.prompt: Why did the rain slow down for a moment?
options: The cloud had run out of all its water
Nimbo felt shy when everyone came out to look
A strong wind had pushed Nimbo far away
The sun had started to rise over the hills
questions.why: It slowed just after the neighbours came out and stared at the sky, and being looked at is what Nimbo fears.

questions.prompt: Why did Marisol whisper "Slow breath"?
options: She was reminding Nimbo of what helps when you feel shy
She wanted her father to calm down and stop shouting
She was out of breath from climbing the ladder
She was telling the rain to stop falling so hard
questions.why: The slow breath is what she told Nimbo she does when she is shy. Right after this, the rain grows stronger.

questions.prompt: How did the well show that the rain had helped?
options: The rope had grown long enough to reach the water
The water in the well had turned a silver colour
The bucket came up full of green corn leaves
The bucket splashed almost as soon as it went down
questions.why: Before, the bucket went down a long way before it splashed. Now it splashes almost as soon as it goes down, so the water is higher.

questions.prompt: What does Marisol do at the very end of the story?
options: She plants more beans in the wet garden
She takes a slow breath and starts to read aloud
She writes a new plan on the back of her hand
She climbs back onto the roof to find Nimbo
questions.why: The next time her teacher asked her to read, she took a slow breath and began.
